# KoHs Inventory Tweaks 1.3.0

Vanilla's inventory bugs fixed, a steadier inventory on servers with ping, faster
enchanted items, and an option to hide the recipe book.

## Supported builds

| Minecraft | File | Fabric API | Java |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 26.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.3.0+mc26.2.jar` | 0.157.0+26.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.3.0+mc26.1.2.jar` | 0.155.2+26.1.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.1 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.3.0+mc26.1.1.jar` | 0.145.4+26.1.1 | 25+ |
| 26.1 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.3.0+mc26.1.jar` | 0.145.1+26.1 | 25+ |
| 1.21.11 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.3.0+mc1.21.11.jar` | 0.141.6+1.21.11 | 21+ |

Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer. Client-side only.

## Fixed, always on

These are bugs in Minecraft itself. They are fixed on every version, with no switch.

- **Double clicks.** Since the double click moved into the mouse handler, a
  double click is remembered after it has done its work. A third quick click
  collected the stack again instead of placing it (MC-306262); placing a stack
  and shift-clicking it moved every matching stack (MC-301852); a drag started
  by the second click of a double click collected instead of spreading
  (MC-312333); and a double click released over another slot collected there
  (MC-311852). Each click now starts fresh after a collect or after a release
  that empties the cursor, as it did up to 1.21.8.
- **A held swap key swaps once.** Holding F or a number key over a slot made
  the key repeat swap it back and forth about thirty times a second, so the item
  ended up wherever the key happened to come up. The repeats now do nothing. The
  drop key still repeats on purpose.
- **Inventory and drop keys on mouse buttons.** Bound to a mouse button, the
  inventory key never closed a chest and the drop key never dropped from one,
  while the swap and number keys always worked (MC-577). They now act as their
  keyboard bindings do.
- **A smooth player in the inventory.** The inventory drew the player as of the
  end of the current tick, so its walk, swing and idle motion moved twenty times
  a second whatever the frame rate (MC-265935). It now uses the frame's moment,
  as the world does.
- **Toggled sprint and sneak on a mouse button come back** after an inventory
  or any screen closes, as they do on the keyboard (MC-308595).
- **Center Mouse Fix in every container.** It now centers the pointer in
  chests, shulker boxes, furnaces and every other screen opened from the game,
  not only in the inventory. After the window changed size, Vanilla opened a
  chest with the pointer 144 pixels from the center in the lab; with the fix, 0.

## New options

- **Steady inventory** (on). On a server with ping, the server answers almost
  every click with the whole inventory, because something else changed it while
  the click was travelling (armor losing durability in a fight is enough). When
  a second click follows within the ping, the answer to the first arrives after
  the second was already shown, and Vanilla flashes that slot back until its own
  answer arrives. Players see a totem or an item jump back, and pressing again
  undoes the first press. With Steady inventory, the slots changed by clicks
  still on their way keep showing those clicks; every other slot, a totem that
  pops, worn armor, an item picked up, shows at once. The server's last word is
  what stays, and the moment the inventory closes, it is all that is left. Nothing
  sent to the server changes. On a local Grim server with the armor wearing down,
  the double re-totem flickered in 4, 6 and 11 of 24 tries at 70, 130 and 200 ms
  of ping; with Steady inventory, in none, and Grim raised no alert.
- **Faster enchanted items** (on). Minecraft redraws every enchanted or animated
  item in menus and the hotbar from scratch on every frame (MC-310555). They are
  now redrawn sixty times a second, which looks the same: the shine moves less

...

# KoHs Inventory Tweaks 1.2.1

**Update if you play on servers with Super Fast Inventory on.** Every earlier
version sends what you do in an inventory it opened early before the server has
been told you stopped moving. Anti-cheats check for exactly that. On an older
version, turn Super Fast Inventory off on servers.

## Supported builds

| Minecraft | File | Fabric API | Java |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 26.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.1+mc26.2.jar` | 0.157.0+26.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.1+mc26.1.2.jar` | 0.155.2+26.1.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.1 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.1+mc26.1.1.jar` | 0.145.4+26.1.1 | 25+ |
| 26.1 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.1+mc26.1.jar` | 0.145.1+26.1 | 25+ |
| 1.21.11 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.1+mc1.21.11.jar` | 0.141.6+1.21.11 | 21+ |

Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer. Client-side only.

## The fix

### What was wrong

Vanilla opens the inventory inside a client tick. That tick releases the keys
and tells the server so: the movement keys are up, the sprint has ended, the
head has made its last turn. Only an input poll after that tick can click a
slot. A server therefore never receives a container click from a player it
still believes to be sprinting forward.

Super Fast Inventory builds the screen between two ticks, up to 50 ms sooner.
Up to 1.2.0, a shortcut or a click made before that tick ran was handled at
once and its packet left ahead of the tick's: a container click from a
sprinting player, followed by the stop and a turn of the head. No Vanilla
client can send that order, and servers that check inventories look for it.

Earlier notes and the wiki said a server could not tell an early opening
apart. That was wrong, and they are corrected.

### What 1.2.1 does

Only the screen is early. Keys, clicks, the wheel and typed characters that
arrive in an inventory opened early are kept until its tick has run:

- The first of them is handled at the first input poll after that tick, the
  earliest moment a Vanilla client could act in that inventory. Each one after
  it follows as far behind it as you made it.
- Whatever you do within a tick of something that was handled late is kept the
  same way, so two actions never reach the server closer together than your
  hand made them, unless a full tick still separates them.
- Each one acts where the pointer was, on the slot that was highlighted, when
  you made it. The pointer itself is never held.
- Once one of them closes the inventory, the rest was made in the world and
  goes there at once.
- If nothing arrived before the tick ran, nothing is kept and nothing changes.

They go through Minecraft's own handlers. Nothing is generated, repeated or
reordered, and nothing is ever handled sooner than you did it.

So pressing the inventory key and the offhand key in one roll still works, and
it lands at the first moment it legally can: what you gain is the screen up to
50 ms sooner and a shortcut that is never wasted on the world.

## Verification

The new `inventory-order` lab records every packet the client sends around an
opening and judges them with the inventory rules of TotemGuard, an open-source
anti-cheat for crystal PvP servers: a click or a close while sprinting or
moving; movement, sprint, aim or a world action with the inventory open; a
click after a close in one tick. Each trial sprints forward turning the camera,
presses the inventory key at a random moment of the tick, flicks to a totem and
presses the offhand key 0 to 42 ms later.

| | Fast re-totems flagged | Vanilla re-totems flagged |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 1.2.0, Minecraft 26.2 | 23 of 48 | 0 of 20 |
| 1.2.1, all five versions | 0 of 48 on each | 0 of 20 on each |

On 1.2.0 it flagged 8 of 8 with the offhand key in the same frame as the
opening, 6 of 8 at 6 ms, 5 of 8 at 12 ms, 2 of 8 at 20 and at 30 ms, and none
at 42 ms. On 1.2.1 every totem still reaches the offhand.

It also presses a second shortcut 8 to 90 ms after the first, 20 times, and

...

# KoHs Inventory Tweaks 1.2.0

## Supported builds

| Minecraft | File | Fabric API | Java |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 26.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.0+mc26.2.jar` | 0.157.0+26.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.0+mc26.1.2.jar` | 0.155.2+26.1.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.1 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.0+mc26.1.1.jar` | 0.145.4+26.1.1 | 25+ |
| 26.1 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.0+mc26.1.jar` | 0.145.1+26.1 | 25+ |
| 1.21.11 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.2.0+mc1.21.11.jar` | 0.141.6+1.21.11 | 21+ |

Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer. Client-side only.

## Fixes

### The highlighted slot and the slot that takes the click

Minecraft cuts the pointer to whole GUI pixels before it draws a screen, and
every slot edge sits on a whole pixel, so the slot it highlights is always the
slot a click at that pointer takes. The GUI Scaler converted that cut pixel to
the scaled inventory and rounded it, which near every slot edge highlighted one
slot while the click, F, 1-9 or Q went to its neighbour. It now converts the
exact pointer and cuts afterwards, as Minecraft does.

The `hover-agreement` lab walks the pointer across every column and row edge of
the player inventory a screen pixel at a time and compares the highlight each
frame drew with the slot a click there would take: 63 disagreements in 560 on
1.1.1, none on 1.2.0, on 26.2, 26.1.2, 26.1.1, 26.1 and 1.21.11.

### Center Mouse Fix in one move

GLFW puts the pointer back where it saved it when the mouse was captured as it
leaves disabled mode, after Minecraft has asked for the centre. Center Mouse Fix
used to read the pointer back afterwards and correct it. It now leaves disabled
mode first, so the request Minecraft makes moves the visible pointer, and nothing
reads or rewrites the pointer once the inventory exists. On Wayland, which
cannot place a free pointer, the release stays as in Vanilla.

### Player Visibility with a transparent backdrop

With the inventory backdrop at 0% there is nothing to reveal, so the
line-of-sight checks for the reveal windows no longer run. With a backdrop they
stop as soon as the nearest visible players are found.

## The Inventory Tweaks page, as a tree

Super Fast Inventory, Center Mouse Fix and Reduce inventory visual motion stay
where they were. Under Super Fast Inventory sits its one sub-option; the mascot
has its card at the end. Nothing here clicks, moves or sends anything for the
player.

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shortcuts follow the pointer | On | Under Super Fast Inventory. Number keys, F and Q act on the slot under the pointer the moment they are pressed. Off, or with its parent off: the slot highlighted in the last frame, as in Vanilla. |
| Zymekoh mascot | On | The cat in every window. |

**Pixel-perfect scale** (on) moved to the GUI Scaler page, beside Affect
Containers: the scale uses whole screen pixels per inventory pixel, so slots
stay even and sharp.

## Animated icons and the Zymekoh mascot

The icons of every tab, option card and warning are now small scenes made of
Minecraft items and particle sprites on a transparent ground, animated and
woken up by the pointer: a slot with a totem in speed streaks for Inventory
Tweaks, a compass for Cursor Landing, a barrier for the Issues Tracker, dyes
that change colour for Customization, a spyglass for the GUI Scaler, an
emerald, a redstone torch or a barrier for the three compatibility levels.

...

# KoHs Inventory Tweaks 1.1.0

## Supported builds

| Minecraft | File | Fabric API | Java |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: |
| 26.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.1.0+mc26.2.jar` | 0.157.0+26.2 | 25+ |
| 26.1.2 | `kohs-inventory-tweaks-1.1.0+mc26.1.2.jar` | 0.155.2+26.1.2 | 25+ |

Fabric Loader 0.19.3 or newer. Client-side only.

## Fixes

### A click could fire when the inventory closed

An attack or use pressed in an earlier input poll of the same tick as the
inventory key stayed queued under the early-opened inventory and fired when the
inventory closed: a ghost hit, or a thrown pearl. Vanilla runs those clicks in
that tick, so an opening with one pending now waits for the tick, as Vanilla's
own opening does.

### 26.2 handled some keys after the inventory

1.0.13 gave 26.2 the key order of 26.1.2. On 26.2, chat, commands,
advancements, social and the HUD toggle are handled before the inventory, so
pressed together with the inventory key they waited until it closed. Each
version now follows the order read from its own client jar.

### Shortcuts after a fast flick in containers

Minecraft updates the slot under the pointer when it draws the screen, so F,
1-9, Q, Ctrl+Q, a click or the wheel used right after a fast flick acted on the
slot the pointer had just left. The immediate targeting that already fixed this
in the player inventory now covers every Vanilla container: chests, barrels,
shulker boxes, hoppers, dispensers, crafting tables and crafters, furnaces,
brewing stands, enchanting tables, anvils, grindstones, stonecutters, looms,
cartography and smithing tables, beacons, villagers, horses and nautiluses.

### Rewritten opening logic

Super Fast Inventory now reaches one decision per input poll, from everything
that poll delivered, and follows each version's own key order. Center Mouse Fix
and Cursor Landing were split into screen classification, landing position and
the opening itself, so each part can be checked on its own.

## A new interface

- **Look.** Dark violet glass with cut corners, a slow background (a turning
  slot-grid sigil, embers and a passing light), section titles over blades and
  lines of current. Cyan marks speed and precision, magenta warnings and
  crimson danger. With Reduce inventory visual motion on, the background holds
  still; hover and click feedback remain.
- **Controls that never move.** Buttons, tabs and screens no longer grow into
  place when they open, and cards no longer lift on hover. The opening scale
  drew each control a few pixels away from where it could be clicked during the
  first third of a second; the openings are now light laid over controls that
  stay put.
- **Switches.** A track and a knob beside the state name, so the state reads by
  shape and by word.
- **Icons.** New pixel icons for every card, tab and compatibility state, sharp
  at every GUI scale.
- **Sharper previews.** The inventory previews are drawn at whole-pixel scales,
  and up to twice their size on the main menu and in Cursor Landing, where a
  larger preview makes a position easier to place.
- **Text that fits.** Card titles wrap between words only, the side columns take

# KoHs Inventory Tweaks 1.0.4

## Supported builds

- Minecraft 1.21.10 — Fabric API 0.138.4+1.21.10, Java 21+
- Minecraft 1.21.11 — Fabric API 0.141.6+1.21.11, Java 21+
- Minecraft 26.1 — Fabric API 0.145.1+26.1, Java 25+
- Minecraft 26.1.1 — Fabric API 0.145.4+26.1.1, Java 25+
- Minecraft 26.1.2 — Fabric API 0.155.2+26.1.2, Java 25+
- Minecraft 26.2 — Fabric API 0.157.0+26.2, Java 25+
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+; client-side only.

## Technical changes

- Added centered GUI scaling for single chests, double chests, Shulker Boxes, barrels, and Ender Chests. Rendering, labels, slots, carried items, hover detection, clicks, releases, and drags share the same inverse coordinate transform.
- Added a dedicated Affect Containers calibration screen. Its preview renders at vanilla 100% while disabled and immediately reflects the selected inventory scale while enabled.
- Enabled Affect all containers by default for new installations. Existing explicit user choices remain unchanged, and Reset restores the new default.
- Added Shulker Box cursor landing with independent persistence and a vanilla fallback switch.
- Expanded Issues Tracker mixin metadata scanning and added an explicit Inventory Scale Fix adaptation without treating unconfirmed conflicts as crashes.
- Added a confirmed blocking rule for Better Screens (`betterscreens`). KoHs disables its gameplay mixins and skips normal runtime registration before showing the close-only incompatibility screen because both mods transform container rendering, GUI scale state, and mouse-coordinate conversion.
- Added the maintained Minecraft 26.2 source/build target and synchronized the feature across every supported version.
